issues.body: `_branch_is_statically_dead` still treats every expression rejected by `ast.literal_eval` as potentially live. Consequently, certainly-false guards such as `if not True:`, `if 1 == 0:`, and `while False or False:` remain accepted. `_live_nodes` also recursively traverses all `except` handlers, so a counter in `try: pass` / `except Exception:` is certified although that handler cannot execute. In each case `_escalation_call_site` can return `dispatch` while no escalation increments `defer_reasons`. The new eleven mutants cover literal guards and nested scopes but still omit both reachability holes identified in round 4.
issues.fix_hint: Conservatively reject regions not proven to execute, including foldable boolean/comparison guards and exception handlers without a proven path; alternatively require the counter in the exact direct production loop-body structure. Add parseable production-source mutants placing the counter under `if not True:` and inside a never-entered `except` handler, and assert `_escalation_call_site` returns `None` for both.
issues.title: Call-site proof still accepts counters in statically unreachable control flow

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major remains unchanged. `_branch_is_statically_dead` still delegates constant folding exclusively to `ast.literal_eval`, which does not prove constant boolean/comparison expressions such as `not True`, `1 == 0`, or `False or False` dead. `_live_nodes` also still descends into every exception handler without establishing that the handler can execute. Thus the structural seam can certify `dispatch` even when the only counter is statically unreachable. The expanded mutant list still omits both specifically reported shapes, so progress is `stagnant`.
